styles.label: Food
styles.blurb: Street bowls, markets and coffee from dawn to late.

styles.label: History
styles.blurb: War sites, temples and the old Saigon core.

styles.label: Shopping
styles.blurb: Markets, malls and craft shops in District 1.

stays.why: Walk to Ben Thanh Market, the river and the main sights; Metro Line 1 starts here.
Backpacker strip with the cheapest beds, tour desks and late-night food.
Quieter streets, local cafés and a short ride to District 1 sights.
Modern riverside area with malls and family hotels; far from the old city, so plan on taxis.

food: Start with pho for breakfast; a bowl at a local stall is often 40,000-70,000 VND.
Try banh mi, com tam (broken rice) and bun bo Hue; street stalls are cheap, roughly 30,000-60,000 VND a dish.
Vietnamese coffee is strong: ca phe sua da (iced with condensed milk) costs about 20,000-45,000 VND.
Eat at busy stalls with high turnover. Drink bottled or filtered water; skip ice if you have a sensitive stomach.
Book a street-food walk or a cooking class early in the trip; check prices and reviews before you book.
more_time: Swap a city day for the Cu Chi tunnels; book a tour or go by bus, and check the day's schedule.
Take the Saigon Waterbus to Thu Duc for a cheap river ride and a different view of the city.
Add a Mekong Delta day trip to My Tho or Ben Tre; long bus rides, so start early.

recommend.why: Two nights covers the war sites, Ben Thanh and a street-food crawl; add a night for a Cu Chi or Mekong day trip.

month_notes: Jan: dry and warm, 32°C days and 23°C nights; one of the best months to walk the city.
Feb: the driest month, about 3 rain days; hot at 34°C, so sightsee early.
Mar: very hot at 35°C and still dry; carry water and plan indoor breaks.
Apr: 35°C highs and rain days jump to about 11; start outdoor plans early.
May: the wet season starts, about 25 rain days; expect heavy afternoon showers.
Jun: very wet, about 27 rain days; keep a rain jacket and a flexible plan.
Jul: the wettest stretch, about 29 rain days; showers usually pass, but streets can flood.
Aug: still very wet, about 29 rain days; indoor sights and cafés are good backups.
Sep: wet, about 29 rain days, with highs around 31°C; check forecasts daily.
Oct: rain eases slightly to about 28 days; still carry an umbrella.
Nov: rain days drop to about 19; a good shoulder month with 31°C highs.
Dec: drier again, about 10 rain days; comfortable for walking and markets.

climate_guide.summary: Tropical city: hot all year, with a dry season roughly December to April and a very wet season from May to October.

items.title: Best time: December to March
items.text: Highs 31-34°C, lows 23-25°C and only 3-10 rain days a month. Best for walking and markets.

items.title: Wet season: May to October
items.text: 25-29 rain days a month. Showers are often heavy but short; streets can flood.

items.title: Hot year-round
items.text: Highs stay 30-35°C. March and April are hottest at 35°C. Plan outdoor sights for early morning.

items.title: Pack rain gear in the wet months
items.text: A light rain jacket or umbrella helps from May to October. Wear quick-dry shoes.

items.title: Humid most days
items.text: Lows rarely drop below 23°C. Light, breathable clothes work all year.

items.title: What to pack
items.text: Light clothes, sunscreen, a hat and a refillable water bottle; add rain gear for May-October.

transit.best: Ride apps for most trips; Metro Line 1 for Ben Thanh to Suoi Tien.

modes.text: Metro Line 1 links Ben Thanh Market to Suoi Tien and the Eastern Bus Terminus. Fares 7,000-20,000 VND, trains every 8-12 min, 5AM-10PM.
Green and blue buses cover 170+ routes. Fares 5,000-7,000 VND local, 10,000-50,000 VND intercity. Tap a contactless Visa or Mastercard.
Grab, Xanh SM and beTaxi work well; fares are fixed and often cheaper than street taxis. Use Mai Linh or Vinasun metered taxis and check the meter is on.
Xe om are everywhere. Agree a price first or book via app; short hops about 20,000 VND.
Saigon Waterbus runs on the Saigon River from District 1 to Thu Duc. A cheap river ride.
Not practical for visitors; traffic is heavy and parking is hard. Use apps and the metro instead.
Fine for short blocks, but long walks are impractical in the heat. Use a ride for anything far.
